samples.summary: New user-input-driven regexes (`BARE_BOX_RE`, `QUOTE_RE`) run per keystroke/per line; I traced them for catastrophic backtracking and found none, but flagging for the record
samples.evidence: `BARE_BOX_RE = /^( {0,3}(?:> ?)*\s*)\[([ xX])\]$/` (checkbox-input.ts:9) is evaluated on the line prefix inside an `EditorView.inputHandler` on every typed space, and `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` (list-commands.ts:~50) on every parsed line. The `(?:> ?)*` group is adjacent to `\s*`, which is the classic ambiguity shape, so I walked it: an iteration matching only `>` leaves the cursor on a space, which no further iteration can consume, so the group terminates there and the alternative paths do not compose — total work stays O(n) in line length for adversarial inputs such as `'> '.repeat(n)` or long space runs. No DoS vector confirmed; no other attacker-controlled sink is touched by this change (`aria-label` is written with `setAttribute` from `textContent`, not HTML, and `md` keeps `html: false`; the read-only path still passes no `onToggleTask` and is additionally enforced server-side by packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts).
